text:
Mia Chen: heads-up — customer `AcmeOps` on a Dedicated private deployment is seeing intermittent 401s. They send keys via `Authorization: Bearer sk_...` to the private LB, but Redwood's private gateway sometimes shows the header missing. Repro included below.

Jordan Patel: @Mia can you drop the repro info and which gateway (NLB/ALB/GCLB) they're using? :eyes:

Mia Chen: they're on AWS NLB in front of an Istio ingressgateway (Dedicated VPC). customer says it fails ~15% of requests and then works again after a retry.

Mia Chen: repro curl they used (sanitized):
```\ncurl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED" \\
  -H "Host: private.acme.redwood.local" \\
  https://10.10.200.45/v1/complete
```

Mia Chen: Expected: 200. Observed: 401. Their logs show incoming request to the app (post-LB) doesn't have any `authorization` header at all.

Alex Gomez: do we have any access logs from the ingressgateway around that time? If the LB sometimes rewrites headers (or lowercases), envoy might drop duplicates.

InfraBot: collected ingressgateway access_log snippet for 2026-02-28T14:02:11Z ->
```
[2026-02-28T14:02:11.123Z] "GET /v1/complete HTTP/1.1" 401 - "-" "curl/7.79.1" request_headers: {Host: private.acme.redwood.local, authorization: "", x-forwarded-for: "203.0.113.22"}
```

InfraBot: same trace for a successful request 2s later shows:
```
request_headers: {Host: private.acme.redwood.local, Authorization: "Bearer sk-REDACTED", x-forwarded-for: "203.0.113.22"}
```

Jordan Patel: interesting — successful one has capital-`Authorization`, failing one has lowercase-`authorization` empty-string. That smells like a header normalization or header-splitting behaviour in the path (NLB->Istio). Some proxies canonicalize headers to lowercase; if a pre-auth filter expects `Authorization` exact case it may not pick it up, or duplicate headers with different cases may result in one being dropped.

Elena Ruiz: we've seen earlier issues where AWS NLB combined with some TCP proxies produces header fragments when clients send large cookies, but here the header is small. Could the client be sending both `Authorization` and `authorization` intermittently (maybe a library bug) and Envoy is normalizing/deduping?

Mia Chen: customer says they're using a CDN edge SDK that sometimes injects an empty `authorization` header for health probes. They also saw their health-check path hit the same backend, so maybe the probe runs without token and ends up racing.

Samir Khan: two hypothesis: 1) upstream health-check or internal probe inserts an empty `authorization` header and due to header-name canonicalization the real header sometimes gets overwritten; 2) Istio ext_authz or an EnvoyFilter in the mesh is rewriting/clearing `authorization` for certain source IPs.

Jordan Patel: quick checks we ran: added an Envoy `request_headers_to_add` patch on the ingress to copy `authorization` -> `x-original-authorization` for a minute to see if it's present before any ext_authz. Patch applied, logs show `x-original-authorization` present even when `authorization` was empty. So the header existed upstream then got cleared later in the filter chain.

Alex Gomez: that nails it — something post-ingress is clearing it. Which components run after the ingress? Our ext_authz service (mounted in the mesh) and a per-customer routing webhook. Could be ext_authz receiving the header, returning ok, then the router is configured to drop `authorization` before forwarding to the private gateway for security.

Mia Chen: attaching ext_authz call log sample (sanitized):
```\nEXT_AUTHZ_REQUEST: headers: {authorization: "Bearer sk-REDACTED", x-forwarded-for: "203.0.113.22"}\nEXT_AUTHZ_RESPONSE: status=200, headers_added: {x-auth-check: "ok"}\n```
```
POST_ROUTER_PROXY_LOG: "forwarded headers: {Host: private.acme.redwood.local, authorization: \"\"}"
```

Elena Ruiz: aha — ext_authz sees the header and returns 200. Router after ext_authz is the one with a policy that strips `authorization`. There's a historical security rule we applied to strip Authorization before routing to some internal backends (to avoid leaking tokens to services that shouldn't see them). Looks like that rule is too wide and applies to Dedicated private workloads.

Jordan Patel: can we scope the strip rule to only internal control-plane services? We should whitelist the private gateway service account.

Alex Gomez: suggested patch (EnvoyFilter snippet):
```yaml
apiVersion: networking.istio.io/v1alpha3
kind: EnvoyFilter
metadata:
  name: keep-auth-for-private-gw
spec:
  workloadSelector:
    labels:
      app: ingressgateway
  configPatches:
  - applyTo: NETWORK_FILTER
    match:
      context: GATEWAY
    patch:
      operation: MERGE
      value:
        typed_config:
          "@type": type.googleapis.com/envoy.extensions.filters.http.header_to_metadata.v3.Config
          request_rules:
          - header: "authorization"
            remove: false
```

Samir Khan: we should be careful with MERGE; test on a single ingress first. Also add a safety rule: only preserve `authorization` when Host matches `*.redwood.local` or the downstream is our private gateway.

Mia Chen: temporary mitigation for the customer: 1) have their SDK send API key in `X-Redwood-Api-Key` header (we can accept that) 2) or enable sticky route that skips the stripping filter (we can configure per-customer in the control plane). Which is faster?

Jordan Patel: fastest is to accept `X-Redwood-Api-Key` on the gateway as a fallback (small code change), but that's a longer-term surface. Short-term: update our ingress EnvoyFilter to whitelist the private gateway host so it doesn't strip `authorization`. I'll take the rollout. :white_check_mark:

Elena Ruiz: I'll add an audit/tracking issue and a test in the Dedicated regression suite to simulate empty-header probe races.

SupportBot: created ticket SUP-2026-348 for customer communication and mitigation steps.

Mia Chen: next steps summary:
- @jordan apply scoped EnvoyFilter patch to one canary ingress and monitor 5m for 401 regression (Jordan)
- @alex coordinate ext_authz config review to avoid wide-scope stripping (Alex)
- @elena add test & run Dedicated CI (Elena)
- Support to communicate fallback header option to AcmeOps (Mia)

Jordan Patel: patch pushed to canary cluster at 2026-02-28T14:12:03Z. Monitoring: 10k requests over 30m, 401 rate dropped to baseline => looks good. Rolling to primaries after a 1h bake. :rocket:

Mia Chen: customer notified, accepted the canary plan and will test at their side. I'll follow up after primary roll. Thanks all. :pray:
__metadata_note: This document is a single Slack thread. Messages are in chronological order and prefixed with display names. No title field included per agents.md.
